name: Idaho Precision Machines
old_description: Idaho Precision Machining & Fabrication, Inc. manufactures aftermarket performance accessories for Motorcycles, ATV/UTV, Snowmobile parts along with machining a wide range of food service parts. We pride ourselves on supplying quality American-made products, at an affordable price.
about:
Idaho Precision Machining & Fabrication, Inc. operates from Eagle, Idaho, where it produces aftermarket performance accessories and custom machined components. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its website has been active since at least 2018 and runs under the CE Components brand (cecomponents.com) with direct-to-consumer e-commerce.

The shop focuses on custom machining for powersports and food-service applications. Its product line includes Harley-Davidson components, snowmobile parts, UTV accessories such as roof consoles, boat and fishing hardware, and a range of food-service equipment parts. The company also offers UTV service work alongside its manufacturing operations. The machining work covers both prototype and production runs, though exact capacity, facility size, and headcount are not published.

Customers span the motorcycle, ATV/UTV, snowmobile, marine, and food-service industries. The business sells directly to consumers through its online catalog — showing items such as a UTV custom roof console priced at $54.95 — and likely supplies dealers and repair shops, though specific client names are not listed.

Idaho Precision emphasizes American-made quality at an affordable price point, positioning its domestically produced parts as a value alternative in a market often supplied by overseas sources.

name: Illes Foods
old_description: From marinades and seasonings, to beverage solutions and sauces, ILLES Foods provides custom-crafted culinary creations and R&D expertise to foodservice chains, food manufacturers, and grocery retailers.
about:
Illes Foods operates from Carrollton, Texas, drawing on nearly a century of experience in flavor development and food manufacturing. The company traces its roots back 97 years, built on values of integrity, curiosity, and partnership, though a specific founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company produces custom seasonings, sauces, marinades, and beverage solutions, offering a full range of manufacturing services for both liquid and dry products. Its capabilities extend to custom flavor creation, flavor development, packaging, and labeling, serving as a single-source partner for product commercialization.

Illes Foods serves foodservice chains, food manufacturers, and grocery retailers. Customers include national restaurant brands and retail suppliers who rely on the company's R&D and culinary teams for limited-time offers, core ingredients, and new product launches. Testimonials from procurement, R&D, and culinary leaders highlight long-term partnerships spanning 3 to 15 years.

The company differentiates itself with a "small enough to care, big enough to execute" philosophy, emphasizing trust, transparency, and results. Its core values—operating with integrity, staying intentionally curious, and believing in the power of partnership—guide decisions, and the team aims to function as an extension of its customers' own R&D and supply chain operations.

old_description: Where tradition meets the future. We create hyperlocal graphics that honor the history and traditions of colleges and universities. We specialize in understanding the market that caters to buyers of college apparel.
about:
Image One is based in Little Rock, Arkansas, where it has operated for more than three decades creating graphics and apparel for collegiate, resort, camp, and military markets. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and produces a range of branded merchandise including apparel, stickers, canvas prints, wood blocks, photo frames, coasters, and ornaments. Its stickers feature a laminated, scratch-resistant textured matte finish designed for durability and water resistance. Image One emphasizes hyperlocal graphics that reflect the history and traditions of each client's brand or destination.

Image One serves colleges and universities, resorts, summer camps, church camps, day camps, and military organizations. Its collegiate focus targets buyers of college apparel, while resort and camp clients use custom graphics to commemorate guest experiences.

The company positions its hyperlocal design approach as a differentiator, aiming to capture the heart and history of each brand to create souvenirs that evoke nostalgia. The laminated sticker finish and range of home décor products are cited as features that add durability and keepsake value.

name: Immedia Semiconductor
old_description: Our smart security cameras let you see, hear, and speak from the Blink Home Monitor app. Experience HD day and night video, two way audio, motion detection, and more. Get up to two years of battery life* with our wire-free devices.
about:
Immedia Semiconductor, headquartered in Andover, Massachusetts, operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon under the Blink brand. The company focuses on designing and marketing wire-free smart security cameras and related devices for residential and small-business use.

The product line includes the Outdoor 2K+ camera, which delivers 2K resolution and enhanced audio in a wire-free design; the compact plug-in Mini 2K+ camera with expansive coverage; the Blink Arc mount that pairs two Mini 2K+ units for a 180-degree panoramic view; and a second-generation battery-powered video doorbell with an expanded field of view. All devices connect to the Blink Home Monitor app for live viewing, two-way audio, and motion alerts, and they integrate with Alexa-enabled devices for voice control. The cameras are marketed as wire-free with up to two years of battery life under typical usage.

Blink devices are sold directly to consumers and small businesses for home security, vacation property monitoring, and small-office surveillance. The system supports multi-system management in a single app, allowing users to oversee multiple locations simultaneously.

The company emphasizes affordability, ease of installation, and integration with Amazon's Alexa ecosystem as key differentiators.

name: Imricor Medical Systems
old_description: Imricor was co-founded by Steve Wedan in 2006 and along with three Imricor pioneers established in the Twin Cities area. Imricor has quickly grown to be the first and only company in the world to bring commercially viable and safe iCMR products to the catheter ablation market. As Imricor continues to grow and develop this market, its focus is and remains the improvement of ablation therapy for patients all around the world.
about:
Imricor Medical Systems was established in 2006 in Burnsville, Minnesota, a suburb of the Twin Cities. The company was co-founded by Steve Wedan, a veteran of the medical device industry with prior experience at GE Healthcare and Applied Biometrics, alongside three other pioneers. Wedan, who serves as president, CEO, and board chair, launched the venture after running a technical consulting firm, aiming to bring interventional magnetic resonance (iMR) technology to the catheter ablation market.

The company develops and manufactures MR-compatible devices for cardiac electrophysiology procedures performed under real-time MRI guidance rather than X-ray fluoroscopy. Its product portfolio includes capital equipment such as the NorthStar 3D mapping system and the Advantage-MR EP recorder/stimulator, as well as single-use devices like the Vision-MR ablation and diagnostic catheters and steerable sheaths.

Imricor’s customers are hospitals and medical centers building interventional MR labs for cardiac ablation. Early adopters include the Dresden Heart Centre in Germany, which signed the first commercial contract in 2018, Rady Children’s Hospital–San Diego as the first U.S. commercial customer in 2026, and Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, designated a European center of excellence. The company also maintains strategic collaborations with Philips and GE HealthCare to integrate its technology into broader MR imaging platforms.

Imricor positions itself as the first and only company to offer commercially viable, FDA-cleared iCMR ablation catheters, a differentiation rooted in its mission to improve ablation therapy by eliminating radiation exposure and leveraging MRI’s superior soft-tissue visualization. The company states that its technology fundamentally changes the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias by enabling real-time, radiation-free guidance during procedures.

name: Imtron Electronics
old_description: Minnesota-based Imtron has supplied high-quality electronic components to manufacturers across the world since 1988.
about:
Imtron Electronics was founded in 1988 and is headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minnesota. The privately held company began as a supplier of high-quality electronic components to manufacturers across the United States and globally.

Operating as a stocking distributor, Imtron maintains inventory from a roster of supplier partners that includes LEMO connectors, Magtech LED drivers, TXC crystals, Henkel thermal management products, and Mornsun power supplies. The product range spans connectors, crystals, thermal management solutions, and power supplies, supported by a consultative sales approach and global logistics.

The company serves manufacturers in the automotive, aviation, medical, and military sectors. Its components are specified in applications where field failure is not an option, such as defense systems, medical devices, avionics, and increasingly electrified vehicles.

Imtron differentiates itself through a consultative model aimed at identifying cost-effective solutions for high-reliability requirements. The company cites its ISO 9001:2015 certification and a team with decades of component-sourcing experience as foundations for supporting critical applications.

name: In La Apparel
old_description: Apparel Branders Inc. sewing department specializes in apparel manufacturing. Every stage of garment construction is meticulously assembled, closely supervised and must comply with strict quality guidelines. Our quality control system is designed to yield a defect-free garment that matches your exact specifications. We have a variety of machines and techniques to accommodate many different types of sewing operations.
about:
In La Apparel operates as a vertically integrated apparel manufacturer based in Los Angeles and Orange County, California. The company, which does business as Apparel Branders Inc., specializes in private-label cut-and-sew production and full-package garment manufacturing. While a founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business emphasizes its mission to revitalize domestic clothing production through sweatshop-free, made-in-the-USA operations.

The company runs two manufacturing facilities in the Los Angeles area, including a knitting mill in the fashion district that produces fabrics such as cotton, synthetic blends, viscose/modal, polyester, melanges, organic, and slub yarns. In-house capabilities span pattern making, grading, marking, cutting, sewing, printing, embroidery, sublimation, heat transfer, deboss/emboss, cotton burnout, and reflective printing, along with fabric and garment dyeing. They handle orders from low-minimum sample runs to full-scale production, serving independent designers and established brands with a staff of around five employees.

In La Apparel serves the fashion industry, corporate and uniform programs, promotional products, and the entertainment sector. Clients include private-label apparel brands, corporate buyers seeking custom uniforms or promotional wear, and production studios in Los Angeles that need custom costumes for motion pictures, commercials, and television. The company also works directly with design teams to develop tailored production solutions.

The company positions itself on three pillars: customer service, creativity, and efficiency. It highlights its vertical integration—from fabric knitting through finishing—as a differentiator that shortens lead times and allows orders of any quantity. A stated commitment to sweatshop-free, domestic production and an "Organic Zone" for 100% organic apparel are cited as reasons clients choose them. Testimonials from brand managers and executives underscore on-time delivery and quality consistency.

name: Index Packaging, Inc.
old_description: Index Packaging’s manufacturing facility in Milton, New Hampshire specializes in wood packaging products, including wood crates and wood pallets, both new and recycled. Since we control the entire production process and have our own fleet of vehicles serving New England, we can guarantee your order will be on time.
about:
Index Packaging, Inc. operates from Milton, New Hampshire, where it has been based since 1981. The company was founded in 1968 by Bill and Connie Lander in the basement of their New York home and remains a closely held, family‑owned corporation. Leadership passed to their son Bruce Lander in 1997, and the board today includes Bruce as chairman and family shareholders Connie Lander and Debora Lussier.

The firm designs and manufactures custom protective packaging for fragile or high‑value items, working across three material families — foam (polyurethane and polyethylene), wood (crates, pallets, and kiln‑dried lumber compliant with ISPM‑15), and corrugated fiberboard. Four New Hampshire facilities in Milton, Dover, Merrimack, and Somersworth provide roughly 290,000 square feet of combined design, engineering, production, and warehousing space, supported by a workforce of more than 200 employees. Services extend to vendor‑managed inventory, just‑in‑time warehousing, and a dedicated trucking fleet for New England deliveries plus nationwide LTL, FedEx, and UPS shipping.

Customers span industrial equipment manufacturers, military and defense programs, medical, pharmaceutical, and laboratory sectors, and food and agriculture businesses. The company also produces retail‑focused lines such as foam‑filled apple gift shippers for specialty grocery and subscription boxes.

Index Packaging emphasizes its “Protection by Design” philosophy, citing in‑house design and engineering at no cost to qualified buyers, the convenience of foam, wood, and corrugated capabilities under one roof, and the agility of a family‑owned structure that enables quick decision‑making. An in‑house recycling program diverts foam, corrugated, and wood scrap into secondary markets.
